title: Add menu controls for extracted game data
changes: Add System menu extraction with background phase progress and a logical encoded-file size estimate, plus a persisted default-off choice between ROM-only and ROM with verified extracted resources on the next normal launch. The ROM remains required.
Reuse managed atomic resource publication, storage roots and existing CLI opt-in. Isolated debug sessions and benchmarks retain their pinned inputs.
validation: Linux targeted config/menu/size tests passed after worker and stage changes (menu-rom-data-final-synthetic-retry-1qztx3ew); the final Linux runtime built successfully (menu-rom-data-runtime-build-final-fxcy9ytt).

A protected EUR ROM passed the real extraction test: encoded estimate matched the published files and a second preparation reused the same verified generation; the unit removed its scratch (menu-rom-data-real-eur-3w3ze64a).

Linux/Xvfb with a protected USA ROM exercised the System menu, selected ROM + DATA, showed phase progress and a 21.4 MiB estimate, and launched once with ROM only and once using decoded resources (menu-rom-data-linux-gui-host-stable-tn5q53a8); screenshots inspected.

Initial Xvfb attempt could not bind a sandbox socket. Two host GUI harness attempts missed menu input under load; the visual-open and mouse-driven retry passed. Earlier standalone test attempts lacked ALSA or Wayland development configuration; the combined dependency configuration passed.
limitations: Extraction and resource consumption remain partial, so the ROM is required. Logical file bytes exclude filesystem allocation overhead and retained generations. The EUR debug-build test, including preparation and reuse, took 626.57 seconds; release performance was not measured. Native Windows, physical controller and AndroidPort were not tested; unexpected worker termination feedback was not separately exercised.
